money-and-cost.rate_and_date: A$1 = 0.704 USD (Reserve Bank of Australia, 30 October 2026)
money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: Legal tender: the US dollar has been the legal tender of Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba since 1 January 2011, replacing the Netherlands Antillean guilder. Notes of US$1, 2, 5, 10, 20, 50 and 100 are legal tender; coins above US$1 are not. De Nederlandsche Bank put new ATMs on Saba and Sint Eustatius in June 2026 that dispense US$10 and US$20 notes; the page says the machines accept local and major international cards, and your own bank may charge a fee. The ATMs don't take deposits or give coins yet.

laws.rule: Unlike in the European Netherlands, cannabis is fully banned in Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba: the Opiumwet BES makes possessing, holding or using cannabis or hashish an offence (art 4), with no tolerance policy.

public_holidays: Bonaire: Dia di Rincon 30 April (2027: Friday), Bonaire Day 6 September (2027: Monday).
Sint Eustatius: Statia Day 16 November (2027: Tuesday). Saba: Saba Day, first Friday of December (2027-12-03).
Shared Kingdom days kept in Caribbean Netherlands: King's Day 27 April, Good Friday (2027-03-26), Easter Monday (2027-03-29), Ascension (2027-05-06), Labour Day 1 May, Christmas Day, Boxing Day.
protocol_notes: Bonaire, Sint Eustatius and Saba are special municipalities of the Netherlands and keep their own island days.
